passage:
At twenty, Neelam had slept badly, skipped lectures and stopped answering messages for five weeks. She kept telling herself it would pass. When she could not finish an assignment she had once loved, she went to the campus counselling centre that same afternoon with her roommate beside her. The counsellor listened, said it was good she had come, and booked a first session for the next day.

At twenty-five, Payal wanted help with constant exhaustion and knotted thoughts. She checked that the psychologist she found held a licence, and after two sessions she felt she was not being heard, so she tried another, who suited her better. When she began to feel better, she kept her appointments instead of stopping. One night her friend Lalit told her on the phone that his own thoughts of hurting himself frightened him. Payal stayed on the line, asked whether he was safe right then, and they rang the helpline together. When he said he wanted someone beside him, she called his neighbour, who took him to the emergency department, and Payal stayed on the phone until staff met him there.

qa.q: How many sessions did Payal have with the first psychologist before trying another?
How do Neelam's and Payal's experiences show when and how to seek help?
qa.a: Neelam went to the campus counselling centre after weeks of poor sleep, skipped lectures and a stalled assignment. Payal chose a licensed psychologist, switched for a better fit and kept her appointments, and she treated Lalit's frightening thoughts as a crisis for the helpline and emergency care rather than waiting.

qa.q: What was Lalit feeling on the phone that night?
qa.a: Frightened by his own thoughts of hurting himself, and needing someone close.

qa.q: Why was staying on the line and ringing the helpline a sound response for Payal?
qa.a: It checked that Lalit was safe right then and brought trained help straight away instead of waiting until morning.

grounding: Signs that it is time to seek help at twenty, and choosing qualified help and using a helpline and emergency care in a crisis at twenty-five.
